title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Mehta
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices across the eval harness, prompt set creation and management, model onboarding checks, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML owners, model reviewers, and SREs who participate in model delivery and serving.

Goals:
- Provide a single, actionable checklist for onboarding models into the eval + serving lifecycle.
- Standardize prompt set and benchmark formats to ensure reproducible regressions and quality monitoring.
- Define quantization validation steps that balance cost and quality.
- Describe the regression triage flow and ownership for timely remediation.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all models intended for Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private serving that will be instrumented by the eval harness or used in production endpoints.
- Excludes experimental research artifacts until they are promoted via the model onboarding flow below.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Owner (Model Owner): single point of contact for the model; owns onboarding checklist and fixes.
- Evaluations Lead: ensures eval harness jobs are wired, baselines computed, and dashboards created.
- QA / Applied ML: reviews prompt sets, edge case coverage, and guardrail thresholds.
- SRE/Platform: validates telemetry, KPIs, and rollout policies in the Console.

High-level process (1-page):
1. Pre-onboarding: collect model metadata, architecture, expected sequence length, and perf targets.
2. Create baseline prompt sets and automatic eval jobs in the eval harness.
3. Run quantization experiments with standardized profiles; capture quality deltas.
4. Publish quality guardrails and thresholds tied to prompt sets & CI gates.
5. If regression occurs in CI or production, follow the regression triage playbook.

Onboarding checklist (detailed):
1) Model metadata and artifacts:
- Model name, version, architecture, framework (e.g., transformer-xx, HF format).
- Intended serving mode: hosted/dedicated/private; expected qps and p50/p95 latency targets.
- Tokenization and vocabulary details; sample tokenization script.

2) Eval harness wiring (required):
- Create an eval harness job: name: eval/<model>-baseline-<date>.
- Add prompt sets (see Prompt Set Guidelines) and expected metrics.
- Reference baseline model for relative comparison.
- Ensure outputs are stored in centralized S3 bucket with prefix: s3://redwood-evals/<model>/<version>/runs/<date>/

3) Metrics and dashboards:
- Mandatory metrics: exact-match (where applicable), BLEU/ROUGE (if relevant), embedding-similarity (cosine), and model-level safety flags.
- Latency and cost metrics: p50/p95 token latency (ms), tokens-per-second, cost-per-thousand-tokens.
- Create a dashboard in Console: folder: Applied ML > <team> > <model>.

Prompt Set Guidelines:
- Each prompt set must include: title, description, tags, input, expected output(s), difficulty, and source. Use the standard JSONL schema in the eval harness (one JSON object per line).
- Coverage requirements: 80% common-case, 15% edge-case, 5% adversarial for production-grade prompt sets.
- Example prompt-set entry (JSONL line):
  {"id":"refund-001","input":"I want to return my order #12345","expected":"instructions for returns; polite tone","tags":["customer-support","short"]}
- Version prompt sets when updated; keep previous versions for comparison. Name convention: prompt-sets/<model>/<prompt-set-name>-vYYYYMMDD.jsonl.

Benchmarking and baselines:
- Baseline models: always retain one immediate predecessor and one canonical baseline (e.g., open-model-x-1.0).
- Run A/B and regression tests: 1) offline eval harness (daily pre-merge), 2) canary rollout evaluation (10% traffic for 48h), 3) full-rollout monitoring (7 days).

Quality Guardrails (policy + thresholds):
- Guardrails are tied to prompt sets and consist of metric thresholds and automatic actions.
- Minimum required guardrails before production rollout:
  - Safety violations per 1k prompts: <= 0.5
  - Semantic drift (embedding cosine vs baseline): <= 0.04 average drop
  - Latency: p95 token latency <= target + 50ms
  - Regression delta (primary metric relative to baseline): <= 1.5% absolute drop
- Guardrail actions table:
| Trigger | Threshold | Immediate Action | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Safety violations | >0.5 / 1k | Pause rollout; notify Security | security-and-compliance |
| Major perf regression | >5% | Rollback canary; page SRE | eng-sre |
| Small quality regression | 1.5% - 5% | Open triage ticket; assign model owner | engineering |

Quantization profile & validation steps:
- Objective: reduce memory and cost while keeping quality within acceptable bounds.
- Standard profiles: fp16 (baseline), int8-static, int8-dynamic, q4_0/q4_1 where supported.
- Experimental profile template (YAML):
  profile_name: q8_mixed
  backend: example-kernel
  bits: 8
  per_channel: true
  calibrate_dataset: prompt-sets/calibration/<model>-cal-v1.jsonl

Quantization validation procedure (numbered):
1. Run calibration: 1k representative prompts from calibrate_dataset.
2. Measure latency, memory, and primary eval metric against fp16 baseline.
3. Capture badge: {quality_delta: +/-% , latency_change_ms: +/-, token_throughput: value} and attach to the model's eval run.
4. If quality_delta > 1.5% (absolute) reject profile for production; else, mark profile as eligible but gated by rollout policy.

Regression triage playbook (incident-like):
1) Detection: regression can be detected by CI pre-merge, canary telemetry, or production monitoring.
2) Initial triage (1 hour):
   - On-call triage owner: confirm the regression signal, metric, and affected prompt sets.
   - Record incident in incident tracker: title, affected model/version, first observed, metric delta, sample prompts.
3) Assign owner and severity:
   - Sev2+: page SRE and Security if safety-related.
   - Sev3: engineering-led triage.
4) Reproduction steps:
   - Pull the failing eval run from S3; reproduce locally using eval harness docker image: redwood/eval-harness:<build-tag>
   - Run the exact prompt set with both baseline and suspect models, collect diffs, and attach them to the ticket.
5) Remediation options:
   - Rollback to last known-good version.
   - Patch prompt or guardrail if false positive.
   - Retrain or adjust decoding parameters if model quality regressed.
6) Postmortem and preventative actions: produce a short postmortem (72h) with root cause, fix, and recommended guardrail changes.

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Run a local eval: docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data redwood/eval-harness:latest eval --model /models/<model>.pt --prompt-set /data/promptset.jsonl --out /data/out.jsonl
- Upload run artifacts: aws s3 cp /data/out.jsonl s3://redwood-evals/<model>/<version>/runs/<date>/out.jsonl --acl bucket-owner-full-control

SLOs and thresholds (recommended):
| KPI | SLO |
|---|---|
| Safety violations | <= 0.5 / 1k prompts (rolling 7d) |
| Primary quality metric delta vs baseline | <= 1.5% absolute degradation |
| Canary error rate | <= 2x baseline error rate | 

Appendix: example alert rules (pseudo YAML):
- alert: EvalPrimaryMetricDrop
  expr: (baseline_metric - current_metric) / baseline_metric > 0.015
  for: 30m
  labels: {severity: "warning", team: "applied-ml"}
  annotations: {summary: "Primary metric drop detected for {{ $labels.model }}"}
